overview.headline: Lincoln turned the Civil War into a war for freedom with the 1863 Proclamation

keyPoints.point: Initially the Civil War was fought to prevent secession and preserve the Union rather than end slavery
keyPoints.quote: Initially, the Civil War between North and South was fought by the North to prevent the secession of the Southern states and preserve the Union.

keyPoints.point: Preliminary Proclamation on September 22 1862 warned that enslaved people in rebelling states would be declared free on January 1 1863
keyPoints.quote: That changed on September 22, 1862, when President Lincoln issued his Preliminary Emancipation Proclamation

keyPoints.point: As a military measure the Proclamation applied only to seceded states leaving slavery untouched in loyal border states
keyPoints.quote: It applied only to states that had seceded from the Union, leaving slavery untouched in the loyal border states.

keyPoints.point: Proclamation transformed the war and announced acceptance of Black men into the Union Army and Navy
keyPoints.quote: Moreover, the Proclamation announced the acceptance of Black men into the Union Army and Navy, enabling the liberated to become liberators.

keyTerms.gloss: Presidential Proclamation that declared freedom for enslaved people in rebellious areas during the Civil War
keyTerms.quote: President Abraham Lincoln issued the Emancipation Proclamation on January 1, 1863, announcing,

keyTerms.gloss: Formal withdrawal of Southern states from the Union that helped cause the Civil War
keyTerms.quote: Initially, the Civil War between North and South was fought by the North to prevent the secession of the Southern states and preserve the Union.

keyTerms.gloss: Description of the Proclamation as a wartime military measure that limited its immediate legal reach
keyTerms.quote: Because it was a military measure, however, the Emancipation Proclamation was limited in many ways.

keyTerms.gloss: Loyal slaveholding border states left untouched by the Proclamation because they had not seceded
keyTerms.quote: It applied only to states that had seceded from the Union, leaving slavery untouched in the loyal border states.

keyTerms.gloss: Federal Union Army that accepted Black men after January 1 1863 to expand freedom with every advance
keyTerms.quote: Moreover, the Proclamation announced the acceptance of Black men into the Union Army and Navy, enabling the liberated to become liberators.
